raw_response.rationale: Although the paper's comparisons of public vs. private ownership and regional vs. local service delivery models (Sections 3.1, 4.2, 4.4; Tables 2-3) are explicitly descriptive percentages, medians, and means without hypothesis tests or uncertainty estimates, Sections 2.3 (p. 9) and 4.3 (pp. 16-17) report a statistically significant inferential Spearman rank correlation (ρ = -0.521, p = 0.018, N = 24 regional utilities) linking a narrow rule-type tariff/administrative-hurdle exposure—the number of cumulative eligibility criteria required for social-tariff enrollment—to a household water economic-access/exclusion outcome—the percentage of low-income CadÚnico-registered families with piped water access who actually receive the social water tariff. Higher administrative/eligibility criteria counts significantly reduce low-income beneficiary coverage, fitting SWiM Family C (tariffs, regulation, and administrative rules).
